Özet – Bu araştırmanın amacı, Covid-19 pandemisi döneminde Türkiye’deki üniversitelerin acil uzaktan eğitime
geçişte yaptıkları çalışmaları incelemektir.
Araştırmada tarama modeli kullanılmıştır.
Araştırma evrenini
Türkiye’deki tüm üniversiteler (208 üniversite) oluşturmaktadır.
Her bir üniversite ile ilgili veriler üniversitelerin
acil uzaktan eğitim sürecinde görevli kişilerden (UZEM’de ve Bilgi İşlem Dairesi’ndeki görevliler vb.)
edinilmiştir.
Araştırmada gönüllülük esasına göre 33 katılımcıya (üniversiteye) ulaşılabilmiştir.
Araştırmanın
verileri bir çevrimiçi anket formu (Google Form) ile toplanmıştır.
Araştırmadan elde edilen bulgulara göre en çok
kullanılan öğrenme yönetim sistemleri Moodle ve ALMS’dir.
Üniversiteler tarafından en çok kullanılan canlı ders
yazılımlarının Big Blue Button ve Perculus olduğu görülmüştür.
Yükseköğretim Kurulu’nun derslerin senkron
işlenmesini tavsiye etmesine rağmen tüm derslerini senkron olarak yürütebilen üniversite sayısı sadece altıdır.
Üniversitelerin çoğu daha önce kurulu olan öğrenme yönetim sistemi (f=29) ve canlı ders yazılımı (f=24)
üzerinden süreçleri yönetmeye çalışmışlardır.
Üniversitelerin yaklaşık yarısı öğrencilerin ders devam takibini
yapmıştır.
Katılımcılar, uzaktan eğitime hazırlık sürecinde öğretim elemanlarının eğitimini en çok zorlandıkları
durum olarak belirtmişlerdir.
Anahtar kelimeler: COVID-19, uzaktan eğitim, acil uzaktan eğitim, öğrenme yönetim sistemi, canlı ders yazılımı.
Sorumlu yazar: Serkan Çankaya, İzmir Demokrasi Üniversitesi, İzmir, Türkiye, serkan.cankaya@idu.edu.tr
Giriş
Kriz zamanlarında uzun dönemli planlamalar yapmak ve bu planları hayata geçirmek
zordur.
2020 yılının başlarında tüm dünyada etkili olan Covid-19 pandemisi de bu kriz
zamanlarından biridir.
Covid-19 pandemisi sebebiyle 2019-2020 eğitim-öğretim yılı bahar
döneminde hemen hemen tüm dünyada eğitim kurumları kapatılmış ve çeşitli düzeylerde
karantina uygulamaları başlamıştır (Daniel, 2020).
Bu doğrultuda tüm dünyada çeşitli

seviyelerdeki okullar, öğrencilerin eğitimlerinden geri kalmamaları için uzaktan eğitim sürecini
başlatmışlardır.
Bu vesileyle uzaktan eğitim deneyimi olan veya olmayan her eğitimci ve
öğrenen, aniden uzaktan eğitim yöntemi ile ders vermek veya ders almak durumunda kalmıştır.
Eğitim kurumları ve eğitimciler, derslerin uzaktan eğitim ile nasıl yapılabileceği ve çeşitli
online araçların nasıl kullanılabileceği konularında arayışa girmişlerdir (Karip, 2020).
Bu
bağlamda uzaktan eğitim anlamında dünyanın artık eskisi gibi olmayacağı ifade edilebilir.
Eğitmenlerin çoğu daha önce uzaktan eğitim araçlarını hiç kullanmamıştır (Çetinkaya
Aydın, 2020).
Bu eğitmenlerin uzaktan eğitim ve uzaktan eğitim materyali hazırlama
konusunda bilgi ve becerilerinin sınırlı olduğu düşünülürse, yapılan uzaktan eğitim derslerinde
her şeyin kusursuz bir şekilde yürüyeceği söylenemez.
Uzaktan eğitim kuramsal temelleri olan
bir bilim alanıdır ve başarılı uzaktan eğitim uygulamaları için bu kuramsal temeller göz önünde
tutularak planlamalar yapılmalıdır.
Hatta ideal olanı, tüm eğitmenlerin uzaktan eğitimin
kuramsal temelleri dersini yine uzaktan eğitim araçları ile almalardır (Shattuck, Dubins ve
Zilberman, 2011).
Böylece hem uzaktan eğitimin kuramsal temellerini öğrenecekler, hem de
bir uzaktan eğitim uygulamasında öğrenci olarak deneyim kazanacaklar ve öğrencilerin bu
süreçte yaşadıkları konusunda öngörü sahibi olabileceklerdir.
Daha önce de belirtildiği üzere
bu kriz döneminde bu tür ön çalışmalar yapmak mümkün olmamıştır.
Bunun yerine eğitim
kurumları eğitmenleri sınırlı düzeyde eğitmek durumunda kalmışlardır.
Bu eğitimler genellikle
uzaktan eğitim araçlarının nasıl kullanılacağı üzerine odaklanmıştır.
Öte yandan bu süreçte uzaktan eğitim konusunda başarısız bir deneyim geçiren bazı
eğitmenlerin tutumlarında olumsuz bir değişim olacağı öngörülebilir (Gaeth, Levin, Sood,
Juang ve Castellucci, 1997).
Özellikle teknolojik araçları kullanmada zorluk çeken eğitmenler
bu kategoride değerlendirilebilir.
Eğitim kurumlarının yanlış tercihleri de (öğrenme yönetim
sistemi ve canlı ders yazılımı tercihi vb.)
eğitmenlerin bu süreçte olumsuzluklar yaşamalarına
neden olabilir.
Bu çalışma kapsamında Türkiye’deki üniversitelerin pandemi sürecindeki uzaktan eğitim
çalışmaları incelenmiştir.
Türkiye’de üniversiteler Yükseköğretim Kurulu’na (YÖK) bağlıdır.
YÖK, ilk olarak üniversitelerin 16 Mart 2020 tarihinde 3 hafta tatil edildiğini duyurmuştur.
Daha sonra üniversitelere derslerin uzaktan eğitim ile verilmesi yönünde talimat vermiş ve
2019-2020 eğitim-öğretim yılı bahar döneminde örgün eğitim yapılmayacağını belirtmiştir.
YÖK’ün almış olduğu kararlara göre, üniversitelerin 23 Mart 2020 tarihi itibari ile kapasiteleri
ölçüsünde uzaktan eğitime başlamaları gerektiği belirtilmiştir.
Bu konuda YÖK Başkanının
yapmış olduğu basın açıklamasının bir bölümü aşağıda verilmiştir (Saraç, 2020):

• “23 Mart Pazartesi uzaktan eğitim kapasitesine sahip olan bütün üniversitelerimizde dijital
imkânlar ile uzaktan öğretim süreci başlayacaktır.
• Bu kapasiteye henüz sahip olmayan üniversitelerimiz için de yine aynı gün, 23 Mart
tarihinde kısa süre içinde oluşturduğumuz açık ders malzemeleri havuzu bütün
üniversitelerimize açılacaktır.
• Uygulamaya dayalı programlarda bulunan teorik derslerde dijital imkânlar ve uzaktan
öğretim yöntemleri kullanılacak, uygulama dersleri ise yine üniversitelerimizce belirlenen
takvimin uzatılması da dâhil en uygun zamanda verilecektir.
• Ön lisans ve lisans düzeyindeki bu uygulama ve yaklaşıma, lisansüstü düzeyde de imkân
tanınacak; denetlenebilir olma kaydıyla uzaktan öğretim ve dijital imkânlar kullanılarak bu
süreçlerde de bir kesinti olmaması sağlanacaktır.”
YÖK Başkanı Saraç (2020) tarafından yapılan açıklamada ayrıca üniversitelerin senkron
(eş zamanlı) ya da asenkron (eş zamanlı olmayan) uzaktan öğretim yöntemlerini
kullanabilecekleri belirtilmiştir.
İçinde bulunulan ortamda senkron uygulamaların güçlüğü göz
önüne alındığında üniversitelerin özellikle önlisans ve lisans programlarında asenkron
uygulamalara ağırlıkla yöneleceği tahmin edilmekte olup daha çok etkileşim içeren senkron
uygulamaların da YÖK tarafından teşvik edileceği basın açıklamasında ifade edilmiştir.
YÖK’ün bu kararları doğrultusunda tüm üniversiteler, halihazırda yürütülen tüm derslerin
uzaktan eğitim yöntemi ile devam ettirilebilmesi için çalışmalara başlamışlardır.
Birçok
üniversite bir hafta içinde çalışmalarını tamamlamış ve bu üniversitelerde 23 Mart 2020
tarihinde dersler uzaktan eğitim yöntemi ile işlenmeye başlamıştır.
Üniversiteler, altyapıları
elverdiği oranda “senkron”, “asenkron” veya “hem senkron hem de asenkron” uzaktan eğitim
yöntemlerini kullanmışlardır.
Hatta altyapısı yetersiz üniversitelerin donanım ve yazılım
konusunda ciddi harcamalar yapmaları gerektiği öngörülebilir.
Bu noktada sistemi kullanacak
olan öğretim elemanları ile öğrencilerin eğitimlerinin de ivedilikle gerçekleştirilmesi
gerekmiştir.
Bu noktada gözlemlediğimiz kadarıyla uzaktan eğitim sisteminin tanıtıldığı web
sayfaları, dokümanlar ve eğitim videoları hazırlanarak öğretim elemanlarına ve öğrencilere
duyurulmuştur.
Tüm üniversiteye hizmet edecek uzaktan eğitim sisteminin hazırlanması ve
sistemin kullanımı ile ilgili eğitimlerin verilmesi sadece birkaç gün içinde gerçekleştirilmek
zorunda kalınmıştır.
Tüm bu süreçlerin yürütülmesinde üniversitelerdeki başta Uzaktan Eğitim Uygulama ve
Araştırma Merkezleri (UZEM) olmak üzere Bilgi İşlem Dairesi Başkanlıklarına büyük görevler
düşmüştür.
UZEM’ler üniversitelerin uzaktan eğitim süreçlerinin yürütülmesi için kurulan
birimlerdir.

Amaç ve Önem
Alanyazında Covid-19 sürecinde Türkiye’de acil uzaktan eğitime geçişte yapılanlara
yönelik herhangi bir araştırmaya rastlanmamıştır.
Bu bağlamda bu araştırmanın amacı, Covid19 pandemisi döneminde Türkiye’deki üniversitelerin acil uzaktan eğitime geçişte yaptıkları
çalışmaları incelemektir.
Üniversitelerin acil uzaktan eğitimde neyi nasıl yaptıkları konusunda veri toplamak,
hangi uygulamaların etkili olduğu, hangi uygulamaların ise başarısız olduğu konusunda
tespitler yapmak büyük önem taşımaktadır.
Ayrıca üniversitelerin bu sürece ne kadar hazırlıklı
olduklarının tespiti de önemlidir.
Yürütülen bu çalışmanın üniversitelerin böyle kriz
zamanlarında daha hazırlıklı olabilmelerine yardımcı olacak sonuçları ortaya koyduğu
düşünülmektedir.
Ayrıca uzaktan eğitim alanının önemini ortaya koymak adına “uzaktan
eğitim” konusunda Scopus veritabanında yer alan çalışmaların yıllara göre sayılarının değişim
grafiği incelenebilir (Şekil 1).
Şekil 1.
Uzaktan Eğitim İle İlgili Yapılan Çalışmaların Yıllara Göre Dağılımı
Şekil 1’de görüldüğü üzere uzaktan eğitim konusunda yapılan bilimsel çalışmaların sayısı
yıllara göre ciddi şekilde artmaktadır.
Bu durum uzaktan eğitimin öneminin giderek artması ve
eğitimin vazgeçilmez bir parçası haline geleceğinin göstergesi olarak değerlendirilebilir.
Pandemi dönemi, uzaktan eğitimin önemini daha da arttırmıştır.
Bu pandemi döneminde

yüksek öğretim kurumlarının acil uzaktan eğitim için yaptıkları çalışmaların özetlenerek
sunulmasının alanyazına katkı sağlayacağı ifade edilebilir.
İlgili Alanyazın
Acil uzaktan eğitim döneminde eğitim kurumları, çeşitli öğrenme yönetim sistemleri ve
canlı ders yazılımları (eş zamanlı sanal sınıf yazılımları) kullanmışlardır.
Alanyazında canlı
ders yazılımlarının incelendiği birçok çalışma bulunmaktadır (Herand ve Hatipoğlu, 2014; Işık,
Karacı, Özkaraca ve Biroğul, 2010; İzmirli ve Akyüz, 2017; Lavolette, Venable, Gose ve
Huang, 2010; Schullo, Hilbelink, Venable ve Barron, 2007; Yıldırım vd., 2011).
Gerçekleştirilen bu çalışmalarda Adobe Connect, Big Blue Button, Dimdim (Şu anda yok),
Blackboard Collaborate, Elluminate Live (Bloackboard Collaborate olmuştur), Electa Live,
GoToTraning, Microsoft Live Meetings (Şu anda yok), Openmeetings, Perculus, VMukti ve
WizIQ gibi birçok eş zamanlı araç karşılaştırılmıştır.
Bu araçların bir kısmı günümüzde
güncelliğini yitirmiş veya başka bir isim altında devam etmiştir.
Eş zamanlı canlı sınıf
araçlarının karşılaştırıldığı bu çalışmalarda araçların birbirlerine göre üstünlük ve
zayıflıklarının olduğu belirlenmiştir.
Canlı ders yazılımı seçiminde gereksinimlerin göz önüne
alınması gerektiği ifade edilmektedir.
Örneğin bazı ücretsiz yazılımlarda canlı derse
katılabilecek katılımcı sayısı sınırlılığı olabilir.
Ayrıca kurumların bütçesinin canlı ders
yazılımlarının seçimini etkileyebileceği ifade edilmektedir.
Covid-19 döneminde aniden
uzaktan eğitime geçildiğinden canlı ders yazılımının önemi ortaya çıkmıştır.
Alanyazında Türkiye’de Covid-19 sürecinde üniversitelerin ve diğer eğitim
kademelerinin acil uzaktan eğitime hazırlıkları ile ilgili herhangi bir çalışmaya rastlanmazken
dünyada bazı ülkelerde sınırlı sayıda çalışmaya ulaşılmıştır.
Özellikle pandeminin Çin’de
başlamasından dolayı uzaktan eğitim ile ilgili Çin’de yapılan çalışmaların daha fazla olduğu
görülmektedir.
Zhou, Li, Wu ve Zhou (2020) Covid-19 sürecinde Çin’in ülke çapında başlattığı
“School’s Out, But Class’s On (Okul yok, fakat dersler var)” kampanyası ile yürüttüğü
çevrimiçi eğitimin arka planını, temellerini ve etkisini incelemişlerdir.
Çin’de yaklaşık olarak
270 milyon ilkokul, ortaokul, lise ve lisans öğrencisi çevrimiçi eğitime geçmiştir.
Birçok okul
çevrimiçi canlı ders, çevrimiçi talebe bağlı öğretim (on-demand teaching), TV’de videolu
öğretim yapmıştır.
Acil durumda büyük ölçekli uzaktan öğretimin Çin’de yürütülebilmesi,
İnternet altyapısının tamamlandığını göstermektedir.
Ayrıca öğrenci merkezli bir öğretim
modeli kurulmuştur.
Bunların yanı sıra bazı eğitmenlerin yüz yüze ders materyallerine
etkileşim eklemeden çevrimiçi ortama aktardıkları görülmüştür.

Çin’de yürütülen bazı çalışmalar ise Covid-19 pandemisi döneminde spesifik olarak bazı
ortaokullardaki uygulamaları incelemişlerdir.
Bu uygulamalar incelendiğinde öğretmenlerin
öğrencilere evde çalışma planı gönderdiği ve öğretmenlerin ders materyallerini çeşitli
platformlardan öğrencileri ile paylaştıkları görülmüştür.
Öğretmen, öğrenci ve velilerin QQ,
WeChat ve DingTalk çevrimiçi ortamlarından birbirleri ile bağlantı kurdukları belirlenmiştir.
Derslerin genelde asenkron olduğu, iletişim sürecinin ise senkron olduğu ifade edilebilir (Cai
ve Wang, 2020; Dai ve Lin, 2020; Xia, 2020; Xie ve Yang, 2020).
(2020) ABD’de üniversitelerin uzaktan eğitime zorunlu geçişinin çeşitli
boyutlara etkilerini incelemişlerdir.
967 üniversite öğrencisi ve 111 öğretim elemanından elde
ettikleri anket sonuçlarının ilk bulgularını teknik rapor olarak sunmuşlardır.
ABD’de pandemi
sürecinde kolej ve üniversitelerde 19,9 milyon öğrencinin ve 1,5 milyon öğretim elemanının
büyük bir çoğunluğunun uzaktan eğitim ile ders yapmaya mecbur kaldığını belirtmişlerdir.
Araştırmadan elde ettikleri ilk bulgulara göre öğrenciler internet bağlantılarında sorunlar
yaşayabilmektedirler.
Öğretim elemanlarının sadece canlı dersler yapmaktan kaçınmalarını,
eğer canlı ders yapıyorlarsa ders kayıtlarını da öğrencileri ile paylaşmalarını önermişlerdir.

Bu araştırmada, Covid-19 sürecinde Türkiye’deki üniversitelerin uzaktan eğitim sitemleri
incelenmeye çalışılmıştır.
Bu amaç doğrultusunda gerekli bilgilere ulaşmak için tarama modeli
kullanılmıştır.

Veri Toplama Aracı
Verilerin toplanması için bir çevrimiçi anket formu (Google Form) hazırlanmıştır.
Bu
anket formunda katılımcıların demografik bilgileri ve bağlı oldukları üniversitelerinin uzaktan
eğitim sistemleri ile ilgili sorulara yer verilmiştir.
Anket formu literatür taraması ve YÖK’ün
yapmış olduğu açıklamalar dikkate alınarak hazırlanmıştır.

Katılımcılar
Araştırma evrenini Türkiye’deki tüm üniversiteler (208 üniversite) oluşturmaktadır.
Her
bir üniversite ile ilgili veriler üniversitelerin acil uzaktan eğitim sürecinde görevli kişilerden
(UZEM’de ve Bilgi İşlem Dairesi’ndeki görevliler vb.)
edinilmiştir.
Katılımcılara; WhatsApp,
eposta ve kişisel ilişkiler yoluyla ulaşılmaya çalışılmıştır.
Türkiye’de YÖK’e bağlı
üniversitelerin uzaktan eğitim sistemleriyle ilgili görüş alışverişinde bulunabilecekleri bir
WhatsApp grubu mevcuttur.
Bu çalışmanın yazarlarından biri bir üniversitede UZEM müdürü
olduğu için bu WhatsApp grubunun üyesidir.
Bu grup üzerinden katılımcılara ulaşılmaya

Abstract – The aim of this study is to examine the actions taken by universities in Turkey during the transition to emergency distance education in the Covid-19 pandemic period. The survey model was used in the research. The research population consists of all universities in Turkey (208 universities). Data related to each university were obtained from those responsible for the emergency distance education process (such as staff in distance education centers and information technology departments). In the study, data could be collected from 33 participants (universities) on a voluntary basis. The data for the study were collected through an online survey form (Google Form). According to the findings obtained from the research, the most frequently used learning management systems are Moodle and ALMS. It was observed that the most commonly used live lecture software by universities were Big Blue Button and Perculus. Despite the Higher Education Council's recommendation to conduct courses synchronously, only six universities have been able to run all their courses synchronously. Most universities tried to manage the process through previously established learning management systems (f=29) and live lecture software (f=24). Approximately half of the universities tracked student attendance in classes. Participants stated that training instructors in preparation for distance education was the most challenging aspect. Keywords: COVID-19, distance education, emergency distance education, learning management system, live lesson software. Corresponding author: Serkan Çankaya, Izmir Democracy University, Izmir, Turkey, serkan.cankaya@idu.edu.tr
Introduction
It is difficult to make long-term plans and implement them during times of crisis. The Covid-19 pandemic, which was effective worldwide at the beginning of 2020, is one such crisis. Due to the Covid-19 pandemic, educational institutions were closed in almost all parts of the world during the spring semester of the 2019-2020 academic year, and various levels of quarantine measures were implemented (Daniel, 2020). In this context, various efforts have been made worldwide  
NEF-EFMED Volume 14, Issue 1, June 2020/ NFE-EJMSE Vol. 14, No. Schools at all levels initiated the distance education process to prevent students from falling behind in their education. Consequently, every educator and learner, whether or not they had prior experience with distance education, suddenly found themselves having to teach or take classes via the distance education method. Educational institutions and educators began seeking ways to conduct classes via distance education and how to use various online tools (Karip, 2020). In this context, it can be stated that, in terms of distance education, the world will no longer be the same as before. Most instructors had never used distance education tools prior to this (Çetinkaya Aydın, 2020). Considering that these instructors have limited knowledge and skills in distance education and in preparing distance education materials, it cannot be said that everything would proceed perfectly during distance education classes. Distance education is a scientific field with theoretical foundations, and successful distance education practices require planning that takes these foundations into account. Ideally, all instructors should take a course on the theoretical foundations of distance education, delivered through distance education tools themselves (Shattuck, Dubins, and Zilberman, 2011). In this way, instructors will both learn the theoretical foundations of distance education and gain experience as students in a distance education setting, which will enable them to anticipate what students might experience during this process. As previously mentioned, it was not possible to conduct such preliminary work during this crisis period. Instead, educational institutions were only able to provide limited training for their instructors. These trainings generally focused on how to use distance education tools. On the other hand, it can be anticipated that some instructors who had an unsuccessful experience with distance education during this period will undergo a negative shift in their attitudes (Gaeth, Levin, Sood, Juang, and Castellucci, 1997). In particular, instructors who struggle with using technological tools can be considered in this category. Incorrect choices made by educational institutions (such as the selection of learning management systems and live lesson software) may also cause instructors to experience difficulties during this process. Within the scope of this study, the distance education practices of universities in Turkey during the pandemic process were examined. Universities in Turkey are affiliated with the Higher Education Council (YÖK). YÖK initially announced that universities would be closed for three weeks as of March 16, 2020. Subsequently, it instructed universities to provide courses via distance education and specified that face-to-face education would not be conducted in the spring semester of the 2019-2020 academic year. According to the decisions taken by YÖK, it was stated that universities needed to commence distance education to the extent of their capacities as of March 23, 2020. A portion of the press statement made by the President of YÖK regarding this matter is provided below (Saraç, 2020):

• This approach and implementation at the associate and undergraduate level will also be available for the graduate level; provided that it is auditable, the use of distance education and digital facilities will ensure there is no disruption in these processes.”

In his statement, YÖK President Saraç (2020) also noted that universities could use synchronous (real-time) or asynchronous (non-real-time) distance education methods. Given the difficulties of synchronous implementation in the existing environment, it was anticipated that universities, particularly in associate and undergraduate programs, would predominantly adopt asynchronous practices. However, the press release also stressed that more interactive synchronous methods would be encouraged by YÖK. In line with these decisions, all universities began efforts to ensure the continuation of all courses through distance education methods. Many universities completed these preparations within a week, and courses commenced via distance education as of March 23, 2020. Universities, depending on their infrastructure, employed “synchronous,” “asynchronous,” or “both synchronous and asynchronous” distance education methods. In fact, it can be anticipated that universities with insufficient infrastructure were required to make significant investments in hardware and software. At this point, it was also necessary to urgently train both faculty members and students who would use the system. As far as we observed, web pages introducing the distance education system, documents, and instructional videos were prepared and communicated to instructors and students. The preparation of a distance education system to serve the entire university and the provision of training related to the use of the system had to be carried out within just a few days.

In the execution of all these processes, significant responsibilities fell primarily to the Distance Education Application and Research Centers (UZEM) and to the Information Technology Departments at the universities. UZEM units are organizations established to manage the distance education processes of universities. In these units, distance education is generally provided at the associate, undergraduate, and non-thesis master's levels, and

There is no research in the literature addressing the measures taken during the transition to emergency distance education in Turkey amid the Covid-19 process. In this context, the purpose of this study is to examine the activities undertaken by universities in Turkey during their transition to emergency distance education in the Covid-19 pandemic period. Collecting data on what and how universities implemented emergency distance education, as well as identifying which practices were effective and which were unsuccessful, is of great importance. Additionally, determining how prepared universities were for this process is also significant. It is believed that the findings of this study will reveal results that may help universities to be better prepared during such times of crisis. Additionally, in order to emphasize the importance of the field of distance education, the graph showing the yearly changes in the number of studies on "distance education" included in the Scopus database can be examined (Figure 1). Relevant Literature  
During the emergency distance education period, educational institutions used various learning management systems and live lesson software (synchronous virtual classroom software). There are numerous studies in the literature that examine live lesson software (Herand & Hatipoğlu, 2014; Işık, Karacı, Özkaraca & Biroğul, 2010; İzmirli & Akyüz, 2017; Lavolette, Venable, Gose & Huang, 2010; Schullo, Hilbelink, Venable & Barron, 2007; Yıldırım et al., 2011). In these studies, various synchronous tools such as Adobe Connect, Big Blue Button, Dimdim (no longer available), Blackboard Collaborate, Elluminate Live (now Blackboard Collaborate), Electa Live, GoToTraining, Microsoft Live Meetings (no longer available), Openmeetings, Perculus, VMukti, and WizIQ have been compared. Some of these tools have become outdated or have continued under different names. These studies comparing synchronous virtual classroom tools have identified the strengths and weaknesses of the tools relative to each other. It is emphasized that the selection of live lesson software should be based on specific requirements. For example, some free software may restrict the number of participants who can join the live lesson. It is also noted that the institution’s budget can influence the choice of live lesson software. Due to the sudden transition to distance education during the COVID-19 period, the importance of live lesson software has become evident. In the literature, while no studies have been found regarding the preparedness of universities and other educational levels in Turkey for emergency distance education during the Covid-19 period, a limited number of studies have been identified in some other countries around the world. It is particularly noteworthy that, since the pandemic began in China, there are more studies on distance education conducted in China. Zhou, Li, Wu, and Zhou (2020) examined the background, foundations, and impact of the online education implemented in China during the Covid-19 period through the nationwide campaign “School’s Out, But Class’s On.” Approximately 270 million primary, secondary, high school, and undergraduate students in China transitioned to online education. Many schools delivered online live lessons, on-demand teaching, and video-based instruction on TV. The ability to conduct large-scale emergency distance teaching in China demonstrates that the Internet infrastructure is fully established. In addition, a student-centered teaching model has been developed. However, it was also observed that some instructors transferred their face-to-face course materials to the online environment without adding any interactivity. Upon review of these practices, it has been observed that teachers sent home study plans to students and shared lesson materials with their students through various platforms. It has been determined that teachers, students, and parents connected and communicated with each other via online platforms such as QQ, WeChat, and DingTalk. They presented the initial findings from survey results obtained from 967 university students and 111 faculty members as a technical report. They stated that during the pandemic, the vast majority of the 19.9 million students and 1.5 million faculty members at colleges and universities in the U.S. were forced to conduct classes via distance education. According to the initial findings of their research, students may experience problems with their internet connections. They advised faculty members to avoid conducting only live lectures, and if they do hold live lectures, to also share the recorded sessions with their students. Method
Research Model
In this study, the distance education systems of universities in Turkey during the Covid-19 period were examined. For this purpose, the survey model was used to obtain the necessary information. The study was reviewed by the Balıkesir University Social and Human Sciences Ethics Committee at its meeting dated 02/07/2020 and numbered 2020/7, and was found to be ethically appropriate (Document Date and Number: 03/07/2020-E.26016). Data Collection Tool
An online survey form (Google Form) was prepared for data collection. This survey form included questions regarding the participants' demographic information and the distance education systems of their respective universities. The survey form was prepared in consideration of the literature review and the statements issued by the Higher Education Council (YÖK). Participants
The study population consists of all universities in Turkey (208 universities). The data for each university were obtained from individuals responsible during the emergency distance education process (such as staff in the Distance Education Center and the Information Technology Department). Participants were contacted via WhatsApp, email, and personal networks. There is a WhatsApp group in Turkey where universities affiliated with the Higher Education Council (YÖK) can exchange opinions regarding their distance education systems. Since one of the authors of this study is a director of the Distance Education Center (UZEM) at a university, they are a member of this WhatsApp group. Efforts were made to reach participants through this group. Initially, a message emphasizing the significance of the study, along with the survey participation form, was sent individually to participants. One week later, for those who had not yet participated in the survey, the survey participation link was resent together with another message underlining the importance of the topic. Additionally, the email addresses of the universities’ distance education units and the units managing distance education were obtained, and the survey participation link was sent to them via email in a similar manner. It is difficult to make long-term plans during crisis periods such as pandemics. The Covid-19 pandemic is one such crisis. During this period, universities were forced to hastily initiate distance education processes for all courses. While some universities that were not previously prepared experienced significant difficulties, it can be assumed that universities with the necessary preparations and infrastructure—in other words, those with vision—will emerge from this process even stronger. In this study, the views of participants who are administrators or staff responsible for distance education at universities were sought regarding what universities did during this process and the effects of these efforts on students and faculty members. The vast majority of participants are directors or employees of the Distance Education Application and Research Centers (UZEM) at universities. Since not all universities have a UZEM unit, in some universities this process was managed by other units such as the Department of Information Technologies or by established commissions. The individuals contacted were involved in the operation of the distance education system. 14, No. It is believed that the most accurate information regarding universities has been obtained, as the respondents are individuals who hold significant roles. Herand and Hatipoğlu (2014) and İzmirli and Akyüz (2017) stated that institutions should establish their own priorities and make decisions regarding live class software based on their specific needs. During the pandemic, universities also tried to decide which systems to use according to their circumstances. The most widely used learning management systems in universities during the pandemic were Moodle and ALMS. The most widely used live class software by universities are Big Blue Button and Perculus. Most participants stated that their universities continued with the existing learning management system and live class software during this process. Additionally, some participants mentioned that the ease of use and the fact that the system/software they use is free influenced their choices. The vast majority of participants indicated that they are satisfied with the learning management system and live class software they use and that they would recommend them. It was observed that in about half of the universities participating in the study, students’ class attendance is monitored. However, the fact that some students do not have computers and experience problems with their internet connection has also been among the topics shared on social media. In fact, several articles have been published indicating that the impact of the digital divide has deepened even further during this period. For such students, monitoring attendance in live lessons, in fact, may lead to their failure. Therefore, it is considered inappropriate to impose a compulsory attendance requirement for live lessons. The literature states that if live lessons are held, the recordings of these lessons should also be shared with students (Hammond et al., 2020). The vast majority of the participants in the study stated that large-scale distance education practices implemented during the pandemic should become more widespread. There are no participants who believe that it should not be more widely implemented. Only one participant believes that remote education practices should be used only in mandatory situations. Additionally, some participants stated that remote education practices could also be used to support face-to-face education. In universities in Turkey, remote education programs are generally offered at the associate, undergraduate, and non-thesis graduate levels. In a study conducted by İzmirli, Şahin İzmirli, and Çankaya (2019), it is stated that there are online remote non-thesis graduate programs in Turkey, thesis-based graduate programs are limited in number, and there are no doctoral programs. In the study, the opinions of distance education administrators regarding online remote graduate education were sought. It was observed that the administrators expressed that thesis-based graduate and doctoral programs could be delivered remotely. In this context, it can be stated that with the experience gained after the Covid-19 process, online remote thesis-based graduate programs will become more widespread and doctoral programs will be introduced. In this context, it can be stated that the procedures and principles regarding distance education in higher education institutions should be regulated by the Council of Higher Education (YÖK, 2015). In the study, it was observed that during the Covid-19 process, all universities provided training to their faculty members regarding distance education systems (by offering user manuals and/or videos). Similarly, in a study conducted by İzmirli and Kırmacı (2017) before the pandemic, it was found that most universities offering distance education also trained their faculty members on online teaching competencies. There are also online certificate programs on how distance teaching can be conducted (e.g. Gülbahar and Karataş, 2016). The literature indicates that, in addition to technical knowledge and skills, education regarding pedagogical knowledge and skills should also be provided within distance education systems (İzmirli and Kırmacı, 2017; Vlachopoulos, 2020). Approximately one-third of the participants reported that academic staff were not prepared for the distance education process or that they were unsure about their preparedness. Since the transition to distance education was made urgently due to the pandemic, a comprehensive in-service training on distance teaching may not have been organized. Furthermore, about one-third of the participants stated that students either did not sufficiently understand the courses delivered through distance education or they were unsure whether the courses were understood. Recommendations
Within the scope of this study, the following recommendations are offered to institutions providing distance education, instructors, and researchers:
• It is important for the distance education system used by institutions to be simple, straightforward, and easy to use, in line with the “user-friendly” principle.
• The study revealed that there are universities that have not conducted any live (synchronous) classes. However, within the framework of the equity theory of distance education, it can be stated that in line with the principle that "the more equal learning opportunities are provided to distance learners compared to face-to-face learning experiences, the more equivalent the learning outcomes will be," live classes should also be included. However, it can be recommended that attendance should not be mandatory for live classes. NEF-EFMED Volume 14, Issue 1, June 2020 / NFE-EJMSE Vol. 14, No. It will be important for universities to establish a robust infrastructure for distance education support services and to provide students with continuous support opportunities. In addition, in-service training on distance education can also be provided to academic staff. • It is recommended that the Council of Higher Education (YÖK) develop a national distance education system that can be used by all universities in Turkey. In this way, the large amounts of money paid for such systems will remain within the country and will help ensure equal opportunities in education. • Case studies can be designed to offer a detailed depiction of the emergency distance education process during the pandemic period. • For the evaluation of emergency distance education in universities during the pandemic, both quantitative and qualitative studies can be designed by collecting the views of all stakeholders (academic staff, students, and distance education administrators). Abstract – The aim of this study is to examine the actions taken by universities in Turkey during the transition to emergency distance education in the Covid-19 pandemic period. discourses.translated_txt: Schools at all levels initiated the distance education process to prevent students from falling behind in their education. Consequently, every educator and learner, whether or not they had prior experience with distance education, suddenly found themselves having to teach or take classes via the distance education method.

Eğitim kurumları ve eğitimciler, derslerin uzaktan eğitim ile nasıl yapılabileceği ve çeşitli
online araçların nasıl kullanılabileceği konularında arayışa girmişlerdir (Karip, 2020). Bu
bağlamda uzaktan eğitim anlamında dünyanın artık eskisi gibi olmayacağı ifade edilebilir. Eğitmenlerin çoğu daha önce uzaktan eğitim araçlarını hiç kullanmamıştır (Çetinkaya
Aydın, 2020). Bu eğitmenlerin uzaktan eğitim ve uzaktan eğitim materyali hazırlama
konusunda bilgi ve becerilerinin sınırlı olduğu düşünülürse, yapılan uzaktan eğitim derslerinde
her şeyin kusursuz bir şekilde yürüyeceği söylenemez. Uzaktan eğitim kuramsal temelleri olan
bir bilim alanıdır ve başarılı uzaktan eğitim uygulamaları için bu kuramsal temeller göz önünde
tutularak planlamalar yapılmalıdır. Hatta ideal olanı, tüm eğitmenlerin uzaktan eğitimin
kuramsal temelleri dersini yine uzaktan eğitim araçları ile almalardır (Shattuck, Dubins ve
Zilberman, 2011). Böylece hem uzaktan eğitimin kuramsal temellerini öğrenecekler, hem de
bir uzaktan eğitim uygulamasında öğrenci olarak deneyim kazanacaklar ve öğrencilerin bu
süreçte yaşadıkları konusunda öngörü sahibi olabileceklerdir.
discourses.translated_txt: Educational institutions and educators began seeking ways to conduct classes via distance education and how to use various online tools (Karip, 2020). In this context, it can be stated that, in terms of distance education, the world will no longer be the same as before. Most instructors had never used distance education tools prior to this (Çetinkaya Aydın, 2020). Considering that these instructors have limited knowledge and skills in distance education and in preparing distance education materials, it cannot be said that everything would proceed perfectly during distance education classes. Distance education is a scientific field with theoretical foundations, and successful distance education practices require planning that takes these foundations into account. Ideally, all instructors should take a course on the theoretical foundations of distance education, delivered through distance education tools themselves (Shattuck, Dubins, and Zilberman, 2011). In this way, instructors will both learn the theoretical foundations of distance education and gain experience as students in a distance education setting, which will enable them to anticipate what students might experience during this process.

Universities in Turkey are affiliated with the Higher Education Council (YÖK). YÖK initially announced that universities would be closed for three weeks as of March 16, 2020. Subsequently, it instructed universities to provide courses via distance education and specified that face-to-face education would not be conducted in the spring semester of the 2019-2020 academic year. According to the decisions taken by YÖK, it was stated that universities needed to commence distance education to the extent of their capacities as of March 23, 2020. A portion of the press statement made by the President of YÖK regarding this matter is provided below (Saraç, 2020):

Necatibey Faculty of Education, Electronic Journal of Science and Mathematics Education

792 Examining the Turkish Universities’ Distance Education Systems During the COVID-19 Pandemic

• “On Monday, March 23, the distance education process will begin in all our universities that have digital facilities for distance education.
• For universities that do not yet have this capacity, on the same day, March 23, an open course materials repository that we have prepared in a short period will be made available to all our universities.
• In theoretically based courses within practice-oriented programs, digital facilities and distance teaching methods will be used; practical courses will be offered at the most appropriate time as determined by the universities themselves, including extending the calendar when necessary.
• This approach and implementation at the associate and undergraduate level will also be available for the graduate level; provided that it is auditable, the use of distance education and digital facilities will ensure there is no disruption in these processes.”

In his statement, YÖK President Saraç (2020) also noted that universities could use synchronous (real-time) or asynchronous (non-real-time) distance education methods. Given the difficulties of synchronous implementation in the existing environment, it was anticipated that universities, particularly in associate and undergraduate programs, would predominantly adopt asynchronous practices. However, the press release also stressed that more interactive synchronous methods would be encouraged by YÖK. In line with these decisions, all universities began efforts to ensure the continuation of all courses through distance education methods. Many universities completed these preparations within a week, and courses commenced via distance education as of March 23, 2020. Universities, depending on their infrastructure, employed “synchronous,” “asynchronous,” or “both synchronous and asynchronous” distance education methods. In fact, it can be anticipated that universities with insufficient infrastructure were required to make significant investments in hardware and software. At this point, it was also necessary to urgently train both faculty members and students who would use the system. As far as we observed, web pages introducing the distance education system, documents, and instructional videos were prepared and communicated to instructors and students. The preparation of a distance education system to serve the entire university and the provision of training related to the use of the system had to be carried out within just a few days.

In the execution of all these processes, significant responsibilities fell primarily to the Distance Education Application and Research Centers (UZEM) and to the Information Technology Departments at the universities. UZEM units are organizations established to manage the distance education processes of universities.

Purpose and Significance  
There is no research in the literature addressing the measures taken during the transition to emergency distance education in Turkey amid the Covid-19 process. In this context, the purpose of this study is to examine the activities undertaken by universities in Turkey during their transition to emergency distance education in the Covid-19 pandemic period. Collecting data on what and how universities implemented emergency distance education, as well as identifying which practices were effective and which were unsuccessful, is of great importance. Additionally, determining how prepared universities were for this process is also significant. It is believed that the findings of this study will reveal results that may help universities to be better prepared during such times of crisis.

discourses.translated_txt:
Distribution of Studies on Distance Education by Year  
As shown in Figure 1, the number of scientific studies on distance education has increased significantly over the years. This can be considered an indication that the importance of distance education is gradually increasing and that it will become an indispensable part of education. The pandemic period has further heightened the significance of distance education. During this pandemic, it can be stated that summarizing and presenting the efforts made by higher education institutions in Turkey in response to emergency distance education would contribute to the literature.

Relevant Literature  
During the emergency distance education period, educational institutions used various learning management systems and live lesson software (synchronous virtual classroom software). There are numerous studies in the literature that examine live lesson software (Herand & Hatipoğlu, 2014; Işık, Karacı, Özkaraca & Biroğul, 2010; İzmirli & Akyüz, 2017; Lavolette, Venable, Gose & Huang, 2010; Schullo, Hilbelink, Venable & Barron, 2007; Yıldırım et al., 2011). In these studies, various synchronous tools such as Adobe Connect, Big Blue Button, Dimdim (no longer available), Blackboard Collaborate, Elluminate Live (now Blackboard Collaborate), Electa Live, GoToTraining, Microsoft Live Meetings (no longer available), Openmeetings, Perculus, VMukti, and WizIQ have been compared. Some of these tools have become outdated or have continued under different names. These studies comparing synchronous virtual classroom tools have identified the strengths and weaknesses of the tools relative to each other. It is emphasized that the selection of live lesson software should be based on specific requirements. For example, some free software may restrict the number of participants who can join the live lesson. It is also noted that the institution’s budget can influence the choice of live lesson software. Due to the sudden transition to distance education during the COVID-19 period, the importance of live lesson software has become evident.

discourses.translated_txt: Zhou, Li, Wu, and Zhou (2020) examined the background, foundations, and impact of the online education implemented in China during the Covid-19 period through the nationwide campaign “School’s Out, But Class’s On.” Approximately 270 million primary, secondary, high school, and undergraduate students in China transitioned to online education. Many schools delivered online live lessons, on-demand teaching, and video-based instruction on TV. The ability to conduct large-scale emergency distance teaching in China demonstrates that the Internet infrastructure is fully established. In addition, a student-centered teaching model has been developed. However, it was also observed that some instructors transferred their face-to-face course materials to the online environment without adding any interactivity.

discourses.translated_txt: (2020) examined the effects of the compulsory transition to distance education at universities in the United States from various perspectives. They presented the initial findings from survey results obtained from 967 university students and 111 faculty members as a technical report. They stated that during the pandemic, the vast majority of the 19.9 million students and 1.5 million faculty members at colleges and universities in the U.S. were forced to conduct classes via distance education. discourses.translated_txt: There is a WhatsApp group in Turkey where universities affiliated with the Higher Education Council (YÖK) can exchange opinions regarding their distance education systems. Since one of the authors of this study is a director of the Distance Education Center (UZEM) at a university, they are a member of this WhatsApp group. Efforts were made to reach participants through this group. Initially, a message emphasizing the significance of the study, along with the survey participation form, was sent individually to participants. One week later, for those who had not yet participated in the survey, the survey participation link was resent together with another message underlining the importance of the topic. Additionally, the email addresses of the universities’ distance education units and the units managing distance education were obtained, and the survey participation link was sent to them via email in a similar manner.

Sonuç ve Tartışma
Pandemi gibi kriz dönemlerinde uzun dönemli planlar yapmak zordur. Covid-19
pandemisi de bu kriz dönemlerinden biridir. Bu süreçte üniversiteler apar topar tüm dersler için
uzaktan eğitim süreçlerini başlatmak zorunda kalmışlardır. Önceden hazırlıklı olmayan bazı
üniversiteler çok zorlanırken, gerekli hazırlık ve altyapısı olan bir başka ifade ile vizyon sahibi
olan üniversitelerin bu süreçten daha da güçlü çıkacakları düşünülebilir. Bu araştırmada
üniversitelerin bu süreçte ne yaptıkları ve yapılan bu çalışmaların öğrenci ve öğretim elemanları
üzerindeki etkileri konusunda üniversitelerde uzaktan eğitim konusunda yönetici olan veya
çalışan katılımcıların görüşlerine başvurulmuştur. Katılımcıların büyük çoğunluğu
üniversitelerin UZEM yöneticisi ve çalışanlarıdır. Tüm üniversitelerde UZEM birimi olmadığı
için bu süreci bazı üniversitelerde Bilgi İşlem Daire Başkanlıkları gibi farklı birimler veya
kurulan komisyonlar yönetmişlerdir.
discourses.translated_txt:
Conclusion and Discussion
It is difficult to make long-term plans during crisis periods such as pandemics. The Covid-19 pandemic is one such crisis. During this period, universities were forced to hastily initiate distance education processes for all courses. While some universities that were not previously prepared experienced significant difficulties, it can be assumed that universities with the necessary preparations and infrastructure—in other words, those with vision—will emerge from this process even stronger. In this study, the views of participants who are administrators or staff responsible for distance education at universities were sought regarding what universities did during this process and the effects of these efforts on students and faculty members. The vast majority of participants are directors or employees of the Distance Education Application and Research Centers (UZEM) at universities. Since not all universities have a UZEM unit, in some universities this process was managed by other units such as the Department of Information Technologies or by established commissions.

Öneriler
Bu çalışma kapsamında uzaktan eğitim veren kurumlara, eğitmenlere ve araştırmacılara
aşağıdaki öneriler sunulmuştur:
• Kurumların kullanacağı uzaktan eğitim sisteminin basit, sade ve kullanım kolaylığına
sahip olması “kullanıcı dostu” ilkesi açısından önem arz etmektedir. • Araştırmada hiç canlı ders (senkron ders) yapmayan üniversitelerin olduğu görülmüştür.
discourses.translated_txt:
Recommendations
Within the scope of this study, the following recommendations are offered to institutions providing distance education, instructors, and researchers:
• It is important for the distance education system used by institutions to be simple, straightforward, and easy to use, in line with the “user-friendly” principle.
• The study revealed that there are universities that have not conducted any live (synchronous) classes.
